# Change a public API

Runifold 0.10.1 · Audience: contributor.

## Goal

Change a public API through the canonical runtime contracts.

## Use this API

`Owning crate export → facade export → executable contract`

Dependencies / prerequisites (use the same Runifold release family):

- runifold with runtime
- runifold-testkit and futures-executor for the offline source test

## Minimal example

The following is extracted from [the compiled source](../../../crates/runifold-agent/src/agent/tests.rs).
Excerpts may use imports, fixtures and helper types from that file; use the complete
source for a runnable example. Test-only assertions and mocks are not application setup.

```rust
fn ergonomic_prompt_grants_registered_tools_and_returns_text() {
    let model = ScriptedModel::new();
    model.enqueue(response_events(
        "one",
        vec![tool_call("call_1", "echo", json!({"value": 7}))],
        FinishReason::ToolCalls,
    ));
    model.enqueue(response_events(
        "two",
        vec![ContentPart::text("done")],
        FinishReason::Stop,
    ));
    let agent = Agent::builder("worker", Arc::new(model), ModelRef::new("test", "scripted"))
        .tool(EchoTool::new())
        .build()
        .unwrap();

    let outcome = futures_executor::block_on(agent.prompt("start")).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(outcome.text(), "done");
    assert_eq!(outcome.turns, 2);
    assert_eq!(outcome.tool_calls, 1);
}
```

## Production example

Use the public-surface test style shown here to define behavior, then add or change the owning API, explicit facade exports, rustdoc, changelog and the relevant RFC. Review semver compatibility; before 1.0 an incompatible public change needs a new minor release. Use scripts/semver-check.sh with the required release history/tool installed.

## Runtime path

Public caller → owning crate API → existing canonical implementation; facade re-exports preserve that path

Preserve the owning crate's canonical execution and authority checks. The full
source linked above provides the executable context; related contracts explain
production persistence and failure boundaries.

## Do not do this

- Do not publish an internal helper solely to make a test compile.
- Do not claim compatibility from compilation of the new version alone.
